OBSERVATION 4
Procedures designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be
sterile are not established and followed.
Specifically,
A. While observing the setup and filling operations on the filling line, the following deficiencies
in the aseptic processes were noted:
i. During installation of the filling stations the operator was observed handling unprotected
sterile parts with gloved hands. These components are positioned directly above the exposed
product during the filling and stoppering process.
B. Your visual inspection program does not provide adequate assurance that finished products
possess their purported quality attributes. Specifically, containers with foreign matter
are not classified as critical defects, despite their potential to compromise container integrity
and to create a risk of microbial contamination of
the sterile product.

C. Aseptic personnel qualification does not require the inclusion of all critical interventions during
aseptic process simulation (media fill). No evaluation was conducted to verify that each certified
operator performed the interventions during a media fill.
D. Your firm lacks adequate assurance that critical process equipment used for sterile drug
product manufacture is maintained in a validated state.
Observation 5
Written records of unexplained discrepancies do not always contain a thorough investigation.
Specifically,
A. You implemented a quality system update for management of laboratory events and deviation
records are no longer opened for unplanned departures from specification.
